item.title: Why was Kick streamer JohnWhatsGoingOn slapped during Vietnam 7-Eleven livestream?
item.description: While livestreaming from a Vietnam 7-Eleven, streamer JohnWhatsGoingOn found himself in a contentious situation when he recorded an Indian man without permission. The man expressed his discomfort with being filmed, but John continued to record, raising tensions. It culminated in a physical altercation when the man slapped the streamer, who managed to capture the encounter on camera. This incident has ignited a heated online discussion surrounding consent in public filming.
item.dc:creator: Global Sports Desk

item.title: NitroCamden finally meets StableRonaldo in person after Twitch raid changed his life
item.description: On October 3, 2026, NitroCamden and StableRonaldo connected at ComplexCon after an impactful Twitch raid that drastically altered Camden's streaming journey. What once began as a modest channel with just one viewer exploded overnight, amassing 100,000 followers in 24 hours. While Camden encountered personal hurdles amidst this rapid rise, their meeting represents a pivotal moment, marking the beginning of a promising chapter in his streaming career.
item.dc:creator: Global Sports Desk

item.title: Malena Tudi to address viral claims about her divorce from Nmplol after months away from internet
item.description: Malena Tudi is gearing up for her return to Twitch to clarify misleading narratives surrounding her divorce from Nick 'Nmplol' Polom. She highlighted the significance of dispelling false information that has impacted her personal life and integrity. Tudi aims to approach the situation with care to mitigate any further negative fallout.

item.title: Pewdiepie’s Ajax Ai Model: YouTuber unveils local assistant on Qwen3.5-9B; OpenAI account suspensions loom
item.description: PewDiePie has unveiled Ajax, a smaller AI model designed to run locally through his self-hosted Odysseus workspace. The project follows his claim that OpenAI suspended his account twice during development, with one displayed email citing “distillation.” Built on Alibaba’s Qwen3.5-9B, Ajax aims to handle everyday tasks while offering a less restrictive experience. However, the model remains unfinished, with benchmarks, hardware requirements and downloadable weights yet to be released.
item.dc:creator: Global Sports Desk

item.title: Brazil election: Lula, Flavio Bolsonaro head to runoff after tight first-round vote
item.description: Brazilian President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva and Senator Flavio Bolsonaro will face each other in a runoff election. Neither candidate obtained the majority required during the first round of voting. The runoff election is scheduled for October 25, 2026, with major issues such as corruption and cost of living impacting the campaign. Both candidates are expected to appeal to voters from eliminated candidates.
item.dc:creator: Yashasvi Vasistha

item.title: India's political will needed to extradite Sheikh Hasina: Bangladesh
item.description: Bangladesh is optimistic that India will expedite the extradition process for former PM Sheikh Hasina. Indian high commissioner Dinesh Trivedi stated that legal processes are currently in motion. State Minister Shama Obaed Islam emphasized the importance of political will from both nations. Meanwhile, outgoing Bangladeshi high commissioner Riaz Hamidullah met with Indian External Affairs Minister Dr. S Jaishankar to discuss mutual interests.
item.dc:creator: Ahsan Tasnim

item.title: Flydubai co-pilot allegedly tried to crash plane after hijack attempt failed
item.description: An Omani co-pilot attacked the captain of a flydubai flight bound for Tel Aviv. Following the assault, he attempted to crash the aircraft into the Saudi desert. Investigators are looking into whether the co-pilot cut the engines' fuel supply during this crisis. Emergency codes were transmitted to air traffic control indicating both a general emergency and a suspected hijacking.
item.dc:creator: Yashasvi Vasistha

item.title: US withdraws all bombers from UK's Fairford base after suspected terror plot
item.description: The United States has withdrawn all bombers from RAF Fairford following an investigation into a suspected terror plot. The withdrawal occurred shortly after several people were arrested in connection with the alleged attack plans. British authorities indicated potential Iranian involvement, while Tehran firmly denied these claims and summoned the British ambassador. Additionally, the US maintains military presence in the Middle East with several ships heading to the region.
item.dc:creator: Yashasvi Vasistha

item.title: 3 million face masks could be used to build 1 km road, Australian study finds
item.description: Engineers at RMIT University have discovered a groundbreaking method to recycle single-use face masks by integrating them into road construction. By blending shredded masks with recycled concrete aggregate, the researchers aim to enhance road materials while tackling the problem of mask waste. Their findings suggest that approximately 3 million masks could be utilized in constructing a one-kilometre, two-lane road.
item.dc:creator: TOI Science Desk

item.title: UK: 2 teenagers jailed for 10 years for arson at Indian restaurant in London
item.description: Two 17-year-old teenagers were sentenced to 10 years for an arson attack at Indian Aroma. The incident occurred on August 22, 2025, when they threatened diners with weapons. Their actions led to severe burns for multiple victims, including a couple who suffered life-threatening injuries. The court emphasized the planning and intent behind the attack, which resulted in serious harm. The motive for this violent act remains unknown.
item.dc:creator: Naomi Canton

item.title: Man’s $3 Goodwill painting turns out to be a 1650 Flemish work worth $190,000
item.description: In a remarkable twist of fate, a former antiques dealer purchased a painting for just $3, suspecting it held greater value. Appraisers on Antiques Roadshow estimated its worth between $20,000 and $30,000, but the auction result astonished everyone, fetching $190,000. This stunning Flemish piece, dating back to around 1650, serves as a testament to the hidden gems that can be discovered in thrift shops and donation centers.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: How farmers are helping reverse farmland wildlife decline
item.description: The resurgence of corn buntings and various wildlife species showcases the power of collaborative conservation work initiated by local farmers. Through the Martin Down and Allenford Farmer Clusters, projects were implemented to improve habitats throughout their farms. This endeavor has led to impressive increases in populations of butterflies and grey partridges over the past ten years. Continued financial investment and diligent monitoring are essential to uphold these successful biodiversity initiatives.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

Meet Nathan, the Texas seventh-grader who turned shellfish waste into a water-cleaning project
item.description: Nathan Gael Montelongo, a seventh-grader from La Joya, Texas, created a project using chitosan. He collected discarded shellfish shells to produce chitosan powder and tested its effectiveness on polluted water. Studies showed that chitosan improved water clarity and benefited zebrafish embryos in experiments. Nathan designed a prototype raft that could automate water quality monitoring and treatment.
item.dc:creator: TOI Science Desk

item.title: Meet the Indian-origin seventh-grader who boosted atmospheric water output by 117%
item.description: Ankith Burki, a seventh-grader from BASIS Independent Silicon Valley, created an atmospheric water generator for his project. He utilized low-frequency sound waves to improve the efficiency of water collection. Testing revealed a 117 percent increase in water production under specific sound conditions. His work earned him a finalist position in the 2026 Thermo Fisher Scientific Junior Innovators Challenge.
item.dc:creator: TOI Science Desk

item.title: Meet the eighth-grader who built a low-cost air sampler to study rural health surveillance
item.description: Bailey Quinn Frank has created a groundbreaking air sampler designed to enhance health surveillance in rural areas. Utilizing basic materials such as fans and filters, this device collects airborne bacterial DNA. Findings revealed notable variations in bacterial composition between indoor and outdoor spaces. As a finalist in the Thermo Fisher Scientific Junior Innovators Challenge, Bailey exemplifies the use of practical tools in tackling public health issues.
item.dc:creator: TOI Science Desk

item.title: Bon Jovi’s foundation helped turn former Army Medical Center into housing for 77 homeless veterans
item.description: Jon Bon Jovi’s Soul Foundation backed a housing project at the former Walter Reed Army Medical Center in Washington, DC. The development opened in 2019 with 77 permanent supportive housing units for formerly homeless veterans. The project was part of a wider redevelopment of the former 66-acre military medical centre.
